_comment: The measured truth about the physical rig. Everything reads this. All values null until they are measured. Bump version and re-measure whenever the rig physically changes: different platform, different guitar, exciter moved, amp gain touched, interface settings changed. Version 0 means nothing has been measured yet.
_platform_note: Bela Gem Stereo (Starter Kit, PocketBeagle 2 base; Bela store order #502852), on hand since 2026-09-10. See docs/ground-rules-and-facts.md 3.1 and docs/phase-plan.md. Earlier measurements on a different rig are tagged to their own profile version in logs/README.md, not carried into this file.
_signal_chain_note: As actually wired 2026-09-11: Epiphone (humbucker) -> M4 (buffered instrument input, direct out) -> Bela Gem audio in; Bela Gem audio out -> power amp (Dayton DTA120) -> exciter (Dayton), straight through, no pedal or other device in between. See ground-rules-and-facts.md 4.5 for the fail-safe decision this relies on: no hardware kill switch, because there is no separate uncontrolled acoustic loop in this build and the DTA120+exciter's worst case is judged safe by Abel.
_spec_disclaimer: Every value in 'host', 'loop' etc. below is null. The Bela Gem Stereo numbers that are known from the published spec (2 in / 2 out, up to 24-bit / 96 kHz, 8 analog in, no analog out, PocketBeagle 2, USB-C) are recorded as _spec_* notes, NOT as measurements. Phase 0/1 fills in the real values.

host._spec_base_board_note: Multi-core. Migration guide asks for safer inter-thread patterns.
host._spec_sample_rate_note: Gem Stereo supports up to 24-bit / 96 kHz. 44100 is the board's DEFAULT project setting, observed 2026-09-11 running bela/io-check-input/ with no rate specified -- not yet the deliberate Phase 0/1 choice (44.1 / 48 / 96 still open).
host._block_size_note: Board default, same caveat as sample_rate above -- observed 2026-09-11, not yet chosen deliberately.
host._spec_audio_io_note: 2 audio in, 2 audio out. Stereo line in; differential line out plus a headphone out.
host._channel_index_note: Confirm by sending a tone to one output at a time and watching the input RMS. On this rig the exciter closes the path back to the input, so one command confirms the channel index and proves the physical chain together.
host._input_buffer_note: Moot for now -- the M4's buffered instrument input sits in front of the Gem's own input regardless (ground-rules 4.1), so this rule is satisfied by construction. Still unmeasured what the Gem's own input would need on its own.

input_signal_check.source: pink noise into the Epiphone's position (guitar -> M4 direct out -> Bela in)
input_signal_check._first_pass_note: Clipping on both channels at default board gain -- source too hot. Abel turned it down.
input_signal_check._second_pass_note: Clean, matched L/R, no clipping. Confirms input signal path end to end. Measured with bela/io-check-input/ (output-silent diagnostic, never writes audioWrite -- cannot drive the exciter). Not the deliberate Phase 1 gain-staging measurement (gain_staging.pickup_into_board_peak_dbfs below is still null).

host._latency_note: Gem spec claims sub-millisecond. Measure electrically by patching an output back to an input. Sets the spacing of the phase-condition comb.
host._spec_analog_in_note: 8 analog inputs, 16-bit, ~22-24 kHz, DC-coupled. Voltage range TBC. Used for the expression pedal (ground-rules 4.3, 8).
host._spec_analog_out_note: None. analogWrite() is not available on Gem. gen1 never used analog out.
host._spec_connectivity_note: USB-C device port for the IDE and gadget networking; USB-A host for WiFi / BT / Ethernet / MIDI; I2C + Qwiic.
host._spec_ide_note: Browser IDE (TypeScript/Vue). C++, Pure Data, SuperCollider supported.

gain_staging.split_point: M4 (buffered instrument input, direct out) into Bela Gem audio in
gain_staging._target: about -12 dBFS peak on normal playing, so feedback growth has room before clipping
gain_staging._ceiling_note: A safety constant in code. No tuning process may raise it (ground rule 1). It must be reviewed for the Gem's actual output level and sample rate by an EXPLICIT human commit before the first live loop - not silently, not by an optimiser. Code is the authority; this is for the log only.
gain_staging._amp_note: Fixed constant once set. Never a variable under test. Wired straight from Bela audio out to the exciter -- no pedal or other device in between (ground-rules 4.5). Set 2026-09-11 (Abel): raw passthrough (bela/gen1-passthrough/) produced audible feedback when the DTA120 gain was turned up; backed off to 12 o'clock, which Abel expects to be the testing point. Not yet a hard-measured unity-gain threshold (see 'loop' below) -- a qualitative listening observation, written down per ground rule 10.5 so it isn't touched as a variable under test.

safety.designated_hardware_kill: none required -- DTA120 power switch available as a manual backstop (Abel, 2026-09-11)
safety._kill_note: Deliberate, not missing: Bela audio out feeds the Dayton DTA120 straight into the exciter, no pedal or other device in between. Ground rule (Abel, 2026-09-11): no dedicated hardware kill is required in this build, because there is no second, uncontrolled acoustic loop (nothing feeds a live guitar amp or PA) and the DTA120+exciter's worst case even at full runaway is judged safe. The DTA120's own power switch is a trivial, always-available manual backstop -- not a required interlock, just there. Software kill (output ceiling, mute-on-error, watchdog) stays mandatory regardless. If a hardware kill is ever added back (e.g. a volume pedal), record it here and it becomes required again.
safety._unattended_note: Not granted yet on this rig. Requires Abel to explicitly confirm the rig connected and permit unattended operation, per ground rule 2.

exciter.model: Dayton Audio (surface transducer, exact model TBD)

loop._note: First feedback heard on this platform 2026-09-11, during the bela/gen1-passthrough/ smoke test, with the DTA120 turned up above its 12-o'clock setting -- not measured or recorded (no frequency, no gain value), just confirmed audible by Abel. Everything below is still null pending an actual Phase 1 session: ramp the DTA120 from silence, find where it sustains, measure the unity-gain setting properly instead of relying on this anecdote.

control._control_note: An analog input (the Gem has 8) - a passive expression pedal per ground-rules 4.3, calibrated from analog_in_voltage_range once measured. MIDI over the USB-A host is available as a fallback.

baseline._note: The 'before' recordings: the loop feeding back with no regulation, at several master-gain positions. None recorded on this platform yet.
